newsitem.title: INDIA: Outlook for Indian shares remains gloomy - Kotak.
newsitem.headline: Outlook for Indian shares remains gloomy - Kotak.

text.p: The outlook for Indian shares remains gloomy due to expected weak first-half company results and delays in implementing economic policies, Kotak Securities, the Indian affiliate of Goldman Sachs, said on Thursday.

"In the short-term the market appears oversold after the steep drop in July and could witness a less-than-sharp rally," Kotak's head of research, Rajashekar Iyer, said in the firm's latest monthly report on India.
"On the other hand, in the light of constraints on the government policy front and weak outlook for corporate performances, foreign investment flows are unlikely to be significant," he said.
"Given the excessive dependence of the market on foreign investment flows the longer term outlook continues to remain bearish."
The benchmark Bombay stocks index has fallen some 18 percent since India's budget announcement on July 22. The index was trading 31.57 points lower at 3073.09 in afternoon trade on Thursday.

Plunging global prices of key commodities and the imposition of a 12.9 percent minimum tax on previously untaxed company earnings are expected to take a bite out of the profits of leading Indian firms in the first half of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March).

"Only significant acceleration of government policy in terms of promoting foreign direct investment or controlling the fiscal deficit could help revive investment demand and keep interest rates and inflation in check," Iyer said.
He said that scenario appeared unlikely as the government currently is focusing on political matters at the expense of economic affairs.
"The current market approach calls for a greater focus on non-cyclicals," he said.

Analysts say the performance outlook for non-cyclical industries appears better than that for commodity-based stocks due to falling global prices of a wide range of commodities and a slowdown in Indian industrial growth.
